articles.title: College Fantasy Football Week 8 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Lineup advice from Eric Froton
articles.summary: Eric Froton offers some help setting those college fantasy football lineups for Week 8.
articles.body:
We are left to cover numerous open spots in our college fantasy starting lineup since there are a whopping 14 teams on bye in Week 8. Here is my start/sit column with an eye on players you can consider picking up if any late-week injuries pop up to throw your lineup into flux.

Baylor led all Power Four programs with 42 passes per game last year, and has continued that trend into this season. The Bears are averaging 42.7 passes, which ranks second to only Cal, to go with 288 passing yards per game, 14 TDs and six INTs. Lagway dropped back 60 times last game against TCU's top-flight pass defense, and gets to play a Kansas defense that is allowing 35 PPG to P4 opponents and ranks 133rd in marginal explosiveness with 18.5% of completions going for 20+ yards (105th). The Bears' aggressive pass game is generating 20+ yard pass plays on 20.5% of completions (30th) with 19% of all throws being 20+ yards downfield. I expect Lagway to unleash 40+ passes and throw for 3+ touchdowns against a Kansas team that has yet to win a Big 12 game.

Iowa State is fielding one of the worst secondaries in the nation, allowing 17.6 yards per successful dropback (134th) with 32% of targets being considered wide open (130th). ISU's 81% tackle success rate is the third-worst mark in the country (88% average), while Arizona ranks seventh in yards per successful dropback and 14th with a 52% passing success rate. Fifita has generated 20+ points in every game this season, averaging a superb 29.5 points per game over his last four appearances. The Cats are favored by 10.5 points and should be able to score 30+ points against Iowa State's reeling defense.

West Virginia ranks 126th in SP+ defense and 137th in yards per dropback allowed (9.1), making them a quarterback's dream opponent. Craig hasn't been a factor on the ground, which lowers his ceiling, but he has thrown for at least 294 yards in four of his last five games. He is an attractive emergency streaming option at just a 2% roster rate against the most fantasy-friendly defense in the Power Four.

Managers are justified to feel trepidation at the prospect of starting the hobbled Lacy after spending a top-five draft selection to acquire his services. He only recorded 16 carries and two receptions for 80 total yards from Weeks 3-6 (which included a bye). Lacy returned to form last week, but only produced 12.3 fantasy points, so his 18-touch workload may have slipped under the radar. With Texas reeling and Ole Miss smelling blood in the water, I expect a 20-touch outing for Lacy and am starting him with confidence despite the unfavorable recent returns.

J'Koby Williams, Texas Tech at Cincinnati

2025 bellcow Cameron Dickey is injured, which has opened the door for Williams to handle the primary rushing duties. He has responded by scoring 13+ points in five-of-six games and ripping Arizona State for 28.3 points last week. The all-purpose weapon faces a Cincinnati defense that ranks 103rd in rushing success rate and just got smoked for 464 passing yards and 45 points by West Virginia. Williams is a must-start and still available in 18% of leagues.

Caleb Komolafe, Northwestern vs. Rutgers

OC Chip Kelly has had Northwestern literally running the option at times, to devastating effect as the Wildcats average 5.6 YPC with a solid 11.0 yards per successful rush that ranks 14th nationally. Komolafe should run all over the Scarlet Knights' pitiful run defense that ranks 131st in yards before contact and 135th in yards per successful rush allowed.

Duke Scott will not play, leaving Gause to shoulder the rushing load against Stanford's almost comically bad defense that ranks 134th in points per drive allowed (3.1) and dead last in red-zone touchdown rate (86%). I expect a similarly heavy carry share as the 21 totes and three receptions that he shouldered in NC State's 31-28 upset of Louisville.

Mosley returned from his month-long absence to set a career high with 13 targets and score 17.5+ points for the fourth time in his four collegiate appearances. In addition to catching a touchdown in each game, Mosley has two carries for 17 yards and 158 punt return yards with a touchdown on special teams, showing his all-purpose utility. He ranks sixth in FBS on a points per game basis, but is still only 42% rostered because teams dropped him during his injury hiatus. If Mosley is available in your league, go get him right now.

Joseph Williams, Colorado at Oklahoma State

Williams was perceived to be battling DeAndre Moore and Danny Scudero for targets, but Scudero got hurt, leaving Williams to monopolize 32% of the team's targets while racking up 35 receptions, 485 yards and five touchdowns over the last five games. This game profiles as a shootout with OSU having just allowed 343 passing yards and five touchdowns to Houston and is allowing 18% of completions to gain 20+ yards. Williams is rostered in 63% of leagues and well worth picking up where available.

Pegan is averaging 16.9 PPG and has seen 11+ targets in three of his last four games. This should be a competitive, high scoring affair between Big 12 contenders, with Houston's defense ranking 124th nationally in explosive play rate (7.7%) allowed. Pegan has scored 23+ points in three-of-six games and should have another fine showing against the Cougars at a 62% roster rate.

Hatcher is quietly the fourth-highest scoring wide receiver in the country, commanding a 34% target share while leading 'Cuse with 74 targets. He has an extremely high floor, having scored 10+ points in every game this year despite having four different quarterbacks throwing passes to him. Hatcher is rostered in 83% of leagues and has to be in your lineup despite the instability at quarterback.

Willie Rodriguez, Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt

Rodriguez has carved out a steady role in HC Will Stein's surging Kentucky offense, having caught five+ passes in each of his last three games, with three "Wildcat" rush attempts to help elevate his touchdown potential. He is coming off a banner day versus Oklahoma, catching five passes for 38 yards and two touchdowns in the 21-13 victory. He should have plenty of scoring opportunities against a Vanderbilt defense that ranks 125th in red-zone touchdown rate (75%) and 111th in success rate allowed.

Terrance Carter Jr., Texas Tech at Cincinnati

Carter had been forgotten about after a pair of four-point games to start the year, followed by an injury that cost him two games. Since returning against Colorado, Carter caught eight of nine targets for 67 yards and a touchdown for 16.7 points. Last week, he received two goal-line carries for three yards and a touchdown in a 53-25 win over Arizona State, as he picked up the short-yardage slack vacated by injured RB Cameron Dickey.

Manning has scored under 25 points in each of his last five games, with a high of 24.4 points in a losing effort against Oklahoma. His rushing utility is nearly non-existent having rushed for 25+ yards just once this year, as his poor pocket presence has led to 13 drive-killing sacks over the last three games. The Longhorns are going three-and-out 34% of the time and rank 124th in plays of 20+ yards (5%). This is despite UT wideouts streaking wide open on 35% of targets, which ranks fifth-most nationally. I simply can't support starting Arch against Ole Miss, as the preseason QB1 has been officially removed from the Yahoo "no-cut" list.

It has been a sad state of affairs in College Station this year, with the Aggies losing three of their four SEC games and Reed's inability to operate from the pocket and throw on time being a primary contributor to the offense's failures. He is still rostered in 37% of leagues and should be dropped after a disappointing 11.5-point showing against The Citadel last week.

I simply don't know what to do with Davison, who is the nominal starting running back for the Ducks, but also lacks the ability to break chunk gains and has lost a fumble in each of the last two games. Compounding matters is the rotating backup QBs we've seen Oregon shuttle through as Dante Moore recovers from a head injury, which has caused teams to load up the box and dare them to make layered throws. Co-starter Dierre Hill handled the vast majority of carries down the stretch against Nebraska, with Davison gaining just 29 yards on 12 carries. Davison could be transitioning to an early-down/short-yardage-only role and cannot be trusted against Illinois this weekend.

Beebe broke out with 24 carries and 203 yards in a 29-23 victory over Northwestern when starting RB Turbo Richard was injured. However, since Indiana bulldozed the pathetic Rutgers run defense 47-15, Beebe has received just nine rushes in each of the following two contests for 55 yards and zero touchdowns. Complicating matters is the return of 2025 RB3 Khobie Martin, who is not listed on the team's availability report for the first time all season. I'm leaving Beebe on the bench against a formidable Michigan run defense.

Kyson Brown, Arizona State vs. Kansas State

Brown is 56% rostered, but has scored 10+ points just one time and hasn't received more than seven carries since Sept. 19, spanning three games. Freshman Cardae Mack has cut into his workload and put Brown on the roster cut line.

The effectiveness of the Oregon passing attack has cratered after QB Dante Moore was injured, with Dakorien Moore receiving 24 targets over the last two games, but catching just 11 of them for 113 yards and no touchdowns. Oregon has officially ruled out Dante Moore for this weekend's game against Illinois, making the entire passing game a red flag. I'm looking for other options after the Ducks managed to scrape together 31 total points combined against UCLA and Nebraska.

Craver missed last week's win over The Citadel with an undisclosed injury, but his star had been fading before that, having produced just 47 receiving yards on five receptions in his previous three games combined. I am not starting him until further notice.

The touchdown-less streak extends to six games as Wesco somehow managed to catch four passes for just 25 yards in a 37-0 annihilation of Charleston Southern last weekend. He has scored more than 10 points just once and is relying on true freshman Tait Reynolds to deliver him the ball, making Wesco a wait-and-see proposition against the Hokies.

Andrews broke out with a touchdown reception and three carries for 26 yards for a season-high 9.9 points last week against Colorado. However, he had just one carry for four yards previous to that with just three total receptions in the previous four contests. TE Noah Bennee is the preferred receiving option, making Andrews a risky bet coming off a rare spike-game.

Wade is still 48% rostered, but that is a relic of the preseason when he was a top-five tight end according to consensus rankings. He has been passed over in the offense and has produced just 4.3 points over the last four games, making him a drop-worthy player.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice for Week 7
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone reveals his lineup advice for Week 7.
articles.body:
Make any day feel like Game Day with the Burger King Game Day Menu. Before you take your first bite, get your lineup ready with this week's must-starts and sits.

Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 7 rankings .

Love has finished as a fantasy QB1 three times already this season, including each of his past two outings.

Next up is a divisional date with a Detroit defense allowing the most fantasy points to quarterbacks. Every passer who has faced the Lions this season has ended that week as a top-seven fantasy starter.

Love also had a huge game in his last trip to Detroit, throwing for four touchdowns and scoring the second-most fantasy points among QBs in Week 13 last season.

C.J. Stroud vs. Giants – With the Texans embracing a more pass-heavy approach, Stroud has been a top-five fantasy QB in two of his last three appearances. Hosting a Giants defense that's the seventh easiest matchup for fantasy QBs should result in another strong start.

Kyler Murray vs. Colts – Injuries to Murray and Justin Jefferson have prevented the duo from suiting up at the same time for most of the season. Fortunately, they finally played a full game together in Week 5 and unsurprisingly it was Murray's best performance as a Viking. Coming off the bye, they'll take on a struggling Colts team that permits the 11th-most points to fantasy QBs and is on the verge of a fire sale.

During his first season and a half in the league, Marks has been an adequate but unspectacular starter when called upon. Spike-weeks are rare for the sophomore, who started in the second half of his rookie campaign and has been back in the lead role with David Montgomery sidelined the last couple of weeks.

However, the coaching staff has consistently praised Marks for his improvement from Year 1 to Year 2 and we have seen him top 80 scrimmage yards each of the past two games — while handling over 77% of the snaps in both contests. The only thing holding him back is a lack of touchdowns, but he found the end zone in the two prior outings. Now, we just need him to put it all together.

The Giants game is setting up to be that spot for Marks. Montgomery is expected to remain out and last week's backup, Jawhar Jordan, has been placed on injured reserve, positioning Marks for a sizable workload.

New York's defense is also one to target. The G-Men have allowed three top-12 RB finishes, as well as double-digit fantasy days to six different ball carriers already. With Houston projected as 10.5-point favorites at home, Marks should have a positive game script and all the volume he can handle.

Ollie Gordon II at Jets – Gordon was impressive in his last three outings before the bye, posting 56 yards, 100 yards and 88 yards, respectively, while scoring a touchdown in each game. That also occurred against three tougher run defenses (Chiefs, Vikings, Bengals). The Jets are the 11th-most generous defense for fantasy RBs, making this his easiest matchup since taking over as starter.

J.K. Dobbins at Cardinals – With four teams on bye and a variety of injuries, Dobbins is getting pushed up the rankings a bit this week. However, the veteran has also been given at least 18 touches in three of his last four games and scored a TD in consecutive weeks. The Broncos are favored by 4.5 points on the road against an Arizona defense that just let both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum finish as top-24 fantasy RBs against them last week.

Jordan Mason vs. Colts – The Vikings have leaned on the run more this season and Aaron Jones Sr. has had to shoulder most of that volume with Mason on IR. However, before getting hurt, it was Mason who led the team in carries (15) and rushing yards (59) while also scoring a touchdown in Week 1. Coming off the bye and facing a floundering Colts squad, Minnesota should control this game. Don't be shocked if Mason earns more touches than Jones, after the 31-year-old's busy month — which included playing through an MCL sprain.

Williams is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 who was heating up before the bye thanks to a six-catch, 102-yard effort in Week 4 and a 47-yard, two-touchdown outing in Week 5.

Now, the Lions return to the field at home to face the Packers, in a game with the highest projected point total on the week (53.5).

In his last two home games against Green Bay, Williams has delivered stat lines of 5-80-0 (2024) and 7-144-1 (2025). I'm expecting another solid performance in this likely shootout.

Germie Bernard vs. Saints (Paris) – Bernard has earned 21 targets over the past two games, while becoming one of Aaron Rodgers' favorite pass-catchers. When a rookie is playing over 90% of the snaps and producing like this with back-to-back weeks with at least 80 yards, you don't put them on your bench. Bernard is a top-24 fantasy wideout for Week 6.

Jalen Coker vs. Buccaneers – Coker is taking his game to another level this season with at least nine targets in each of his three healthy appearances, leading to top-24 fantasy WR results every time. In the past two weeks, the Bucs defense has let two receivers reach double-digit fantasy points in both games. Coker and Tetairoa McMillan will continue that trend.

Carnell Tate vs. Browns – Tate isn't getting the hype he deserves because the Titans are an uninspiring franchise at the moment. However, the rookie is on the verge of becoming a must-start in fantasy with stat lines of 6-58-0, 9-145-0 and 6-70-1 in three of his last four contests.

Higbee was going to be my recommended start even before Puka Nacua popped up with a calf injury on Thursday. We'll monitor the situation to see if the Rams' star wideout will be available, but Higbee is a strong option either way since Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson are already sidelined.

Despite a quieter outing in Week 6, Higbee was on a roll in the previous three contests with 62 yards and a TD in Week 3 (TE7), 67 yards in Week 4 (TE14) and 83 yards in Week 5 (TE10).

Meanwhile, his next opponent, the Raiders, are giving up the seventh most fantasy points to tight ends. If Puka plays, Higbee will be a top-10 option. But if Puka is ruled out, Higbee has top-five upside.

T.J. Hockenson vs. Colts – We're finally going to see the Vikings offense with most of its starters on the field this week. That's bad news for the Colts defense. Indy is a plus matchup for tight ends and has allowed big days to the likes of Travis Kelce and Pat Freiermuth. Hockenson should be a solid streamer this week.

Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. 49ers – Pitts has shown signs of life for three straight weeks with 47 yards, 42 yards and a touchdown and most recently, 60 yards and two TDs, respectively. The matchup with San Francisco isn't good, but we just watched Chig Okonkwo post 7-69-0 on them Monday night. Pitts is in play once again as a low-end TE1 in a game with a healthy 50.5 projected point total.

After starting the season with two straight top-10 fantasy results, Mahomes hasn't cracked the QB1 range in his last three games (QB20, QB13, Q23).

Injuries to his receiving corps and offensive line have been a problem and could be exposed even more when he travels to Seattle. The Seahawks defense allows the fewest passing yards and the second fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks.

It's also worth noting, Mahomes isn't running as much coming off the ACL last season, as was expected coming into the year. After averaging over 30 rushing yards per contest in 2025, he's down to 11 yards per game this year.

Tyler Shough vs. Steelers (Paris) – Shough is a risky player to put in the sit column, given the Saints' uptempo style and tendency to find themselves in shootouts. However, the Steelers are allowing the fourth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks and have only let one QB top 14 points against them this year.

Sam Darnold vs. Chiefs – Darnold has only finished inside the top-15 fantasy QBs once this season and now faces a Chiefs defense that's the third-toughest matchup for his position.

Fantasy managers had the rug pulled out from under them on Friday afternoon when the Seahawks announced that Zach Charbonnet would not be making his season debut in Week 7. That means we'll get another week with the combination of Wilson and George Holani.

Even though Wilson has had some strong performances in his relief starts this year, this isn't a time to get him in your lineup. The Chiefs defense has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards, fourth-fewest rushing TDs and sixth-fewest fantasy points to running backs.

If you do start Wilson out of desperation, you'll need him to find the end zone in order to pay off for fantasy.

Alvin Kamara vs. Steelers (Paris) – Kamara is clearly a declining player, but his veteran savvy has helped him find the end zone and produce as a flex option a couple of times in the last month. In Week 6, Kendre Miller handled the bulk of the early-down work and C.J. Donaldson continued to be involved as a pass-catching option. So, expecting fluky long touchdowns from Kamara is a dangerous path to take.

Cam Skattebo at Texans – It's possible Skattebo escapes the coach's doghouse and bounces back after being held without a touch last week. However, it's more likely the Giants backfield remains a three-man committee with Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary also involved. The Texans aren't an ideal matchup either, having permitted the fifth-fewest rushing yards and 10th-fewest fantasy points to RBs this season.

Tyler Allgeier vs. Broncos – Even with Jeremiyah Love expected to miss another game, it's difficult for fantasy managers to trust Allgeier after he split work with Bam Knight last week. Touches were divided fairly evenly; 19-17 and the snaps weren't far off either at 56%-46%. Allgeier is just a TD-or-bust RB3.

Wilson's production has boggled the mind following Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade to Houston. After producing as a fantasy WR1 last season when Harrison was out of the lineup and posting 11-89-1 and 7-95-0 in the two weeks before Harrison was dealt, expectations were sky-high.

Sadly, Wilson's targets have dropped to just seven per game and the results have been incredibly disappointing, with stat lines of 4-30-0 and 4-32-0, respectively.

The matchup doesn't get any easier this week against the Broncos. Denver is the eighth toughest opponent for fantasy receivers so far this year and might get Pat Surtain II back from his ankle injury.

Xavier Worthy at Seahawks – Worthy has put up at least 70 yards in back-to-back games, but Seattle's defense won't make life easy on him. The Seahawks are 31st in fantasy points allowed to wideouts.

Tre Tucker vs. Rams – Tucker is coming off a huge fantasy performance in an easy matchup with the Bills, but let's not forget his boom-or-bust nature. He's been held under 45 yards with no touchdowns in four of his five outings this year. Now, he battles the Rams, who have only let one receiver op 50 yards against them. This isn't a spot to take a swing on Tucker.

Keenan Allen at Vikings – Things are about to get ugly in Indianapolis. The Colts are no match for a Brian Flores defense fresh off a bye. Minnesota has also kept every receiver its faced over the last four games to 67 yards or less, with just one touchdown to wideouts during that span.

Ferguson remains a TD-or-bust low-end fantasy TE2, whose only upside exists when injuries occur in his receiving corps. After his touchdown eruption in Week 2 and Week 3, Ferguson has been held under 20 yards in three consecutive weeks.

The 27-year-old hasn't reached the end zone against the Eagles since 2023, so I'm not looking in his direction for a spot start this week.

Juwan Johnson vs. Steelers (Paris) – Johnson followed up his 16-yard outing in Week 5 with zeros across the board in Week 6. That makes him impossible to trust in your lineup. With first-round receiver Jordyn Tyson expected to return after the Saints' Week 8 bye, it's time to find a fantasy replacement for Johnson.

Harold Fannin Jr. at Titans – Fannin has been limited to just one catch in each of the past two weeks. Meanwhile, the Titans have held every tight end they've encountered this year to 34 yards or less. That's not exactly a recipe for fantasy success.

articles.title: Could Gary Trent Jr. cap circumvention be worse than Kawhi Leonard, Clippers?
articles.summary: The NBA has closed their investigation into the LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard regarding cap circumvention, and punishments have been handed down. The next le...
articles.body:
The NBA has closed their investigation into the LA Clippers and Kawhi Leonard regarding cap circumvention, and punishments have been handed down. The next league investigation that has been underway and also deals with potential salary cap circumvention is with the Milwaukee Bucks and Gary Trent Jr.

At the basis of the NBA's investigation into Gary Trent Jr. is the contract he signed this offseason with the Bucks for four years and worth around $64 million. Prior to signing that deal, Trent had been on a minimum contract with the team. And if there is anything illegal found by the league, the punishment could worse that what was given to the Clippers and Leonard, as per Brian Windhorst of ESPN.

"I don't know what's going to happen in that investigation. I will tell you that it is a frequent conversation as I talk with people around the league … it is being done by a different law firm than the Clippers investigation," Windhorst reported during a recent episode of 'The Hoop Collective.' "I want to be clear, I want to be cautious, but I had an executive say to me that if this is proven to be true, then this is actually more egregious than the Clippers deal."

Windhorst explained what the executive meant regarding it being worse than the Clippers in that the Clippers did not get any salary cap relief, it was just to get their star player more money. articles.summary: This week's SmackDown put a heavy emphasis on the women's division, with three out of the four scheduled matches featuring the division.
articles.body:
This week's SmackDown put a heavy emphasis on the women's division, with three out of the four scheduled matches featuring the division.

Here's a look at what WWE advertised for Friday's show:

Chelsea Green vs. Roxanne Perez (Women's WWE Championship)

Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley vs. B-Fab and Michin (Women's Tag Titles)

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's SmackDown.

After a quick recap video from Raw, Sami Zayn came out with Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae by his side. Zayn got some boos, which was a little surprising given that the show took place in his home country of Canada.

Zayn spoke about his segment with Reigns and put over his WWE title as the top belt in the company that everyone wants. This led to Rey Fenix joining him in the ring.

Fenix said he doesn't know what Penta will do, but if Zayn disrespects his family, they will have a problem. He and Gargano almost got into it, but Zayn calmed them down. This is when Trick Williams decided to make his presence felt.

There was a lot of trash talk before Williams finally demanded a title shot. Zayn ended up taking a cheap shot at Williams as he was focused on Gargano. Nick Aldis came out and booked a tag match with Gargano and Zayn taking on Williams and Fenix.

This was all pretty textbook stuff, but at least it led to a semi-interesting match getting booked for the show.

Zayn made a little flub during his promo and Gargano hilariously acted confused by his words. It was one of those little moments that would be easy to miss.

Fenix and Gargano would have a hell of a match together.

Williams listing off being married to Lash Legend as one of his biggest accomplishments earned him some husband points.

Chelsea Green vs. Roxanne Perez (WWE Women's Championship)

The first match of the night saw Green put her WWE title on the line against Perez, who was getting her first shot at a world title since joining the main roster.

They locked up and fought in that position for a little while before they started trading counters and holds. They tried to make it feel competitive with some near-falls, while still pacing themselves so they could build momentum over time.

This match felt like a fresh combination, which is always welcome in the world title scene. Green has been great as the WWE champion, and Roxy is finally getting her feet wet in the main event scene after playing backup for Liv Morgan in Judgment Day for the past couple of years.

Raquel Rodriguez pushed Chelsea off the top rope while the ref was distracted, but Iyo Sky ran down to fight her off. Green was able to hit her finisher on Perez to retain the title. As soon as it was over, Morgan and Rodriguez attacked the champion. Tiffany Stratton showed up to even the odds.

Morgan escaped with help from Perez and Rodriguez before Tiffy could cash in the briefcase.

It was surprising to see Perez come out alone, but it definitely made sure all of the focus was on her instead of Judgment Day.

This match would have been much better without all of the shenanigans.

WWE plugged the Street Fighter movie with Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns before Giulia faced Monroe in a Street Fight on SmackDown.

They started fighting before Monroe even made it to the ring, so the ref called for the bell to get things underway. Giulia had a pyramid of chairs she had built next to the ring during the break, but Monroe was able to avoid being thrown into it.

A couple of minutes later, Giulia successfully whipped her into the chairs to send the show into a break. They also brought some kendo sticks and a garbage can into the fight during the commercial.

They fought into the backstage area despite this not being a Falls Count Anywhere match. Monroe was driven into a mirror before being dragged back toward the ring.

They did their best to make this feel violent, but without a single drop of blood, there was only so much they could do. The fact that Monroe didn't suffer a single wound from being shoved face-first into a mirror really emphasized how restricted they were.

Giulia and Monroe did a good job making this feel like a personal fight, but it fell short of what we know these two can accomplish. Monroe scored the win with a Neutralizer.

It's sad that WWE took so long to find a way to use Monroe. She's a great character and in-ring worker, so the delays never made sense.

The chair pyramid seemed prime for a fall from inside the ring, so it was a little underwhelming to see them knocked down with an Irish whip. The suplex onto them was cool, though.

Monroe's sold the stomp from Giulia like she was dead. It was great.

Way-Too-Early WrestleMania 43 Predictions 🔮

From Friends to Enemies to Friends to Enemies Again

Randy Orton came to the ring after the break to talk about Cody Rhodes and what he did to Baron Corbin last week when he punted him.

The Viper said Cody can attack anyone he wants, but it means nothing because hs isn't attacking the one person who matters.

Cody came out and gave a speech about all of the people he has watched Orton betray over the years. He insulted The Viper as officials surrounded the ring, ready to jump between them if things got out of hand.

Aldis booked them in a match at Crown Jewel to settle this once and for all. Rhodes said he would only do it if it was Last Man Standing.

Orton and Rhodes are both capable of keeping the crowd invested, but they had no new ground to cover in this segment. This was just a rehash of everything they had said to each other in previous exchanges.

Tatum Paxley and Alexa Bliss vs. B-Fab and Michin (Women's Tag Team Titles)

Charlotte Flair was unable to be at ringside for Bliss and Paxley's title defense against Michin and B-Fab, but Jade Cargill was there for her allies.

B-Fab took control right away and hit a series of strikes, but Little Miss Bliss was able to tag Tatum and hit a double-team combo in the corner.

All four women made sure the pace was quick, but it felt like they were going through the paces. It should have felt much more competitive, especially since a title change was coming.

Cargill helped with a cheap shot to Paxley, which allowed Michin to hit a Styles Clash for the pin to win the tag titles. The match had good energy, but it fell short in just about every other aspect.

Booking a title change so soon after the last one was also a strange decision, but at least Michin finally has a title after all this time in WWE without one.

Result: B-Fab and Michin defeated Bliss and Paxley

B-Fab spinning corner kick looked way too slow to be effective.

It feels like they took the tag titles off Fatal Influence too quickly. Having all three women holding titles made them feel important.

Shinsuke Nakamura and Kyoki got another shot at Tama and Talla Tonga this week, but before their match could begin, Kyoki stole Haku's walking stick.

A fight broke out in the aisle, and officials scurried out from the back in a futile attempt to break it up. The match never ended up happening because they couldn't get them to stop fighting.

Michael Cole and Corey Graves then plugged new merch from Danhausen as the fight continued near the stage. It was a strange way to end the segment.

Rey Fenix, Penta and Trick Williams vs. Sami Zayn, Ricky Saints and Johnny Gargano

CM Punk and Kevin Owens had a backstage segment with Aldis to hype their upcoming match.

The main event was the tag match that was booked in the opening segment with Fenix and Williams taking on Zayn and Gargano.

The match barely got started when Ricky Saints showed up and attacked Fenix to cause a disqualification. Penta came out to make the save and proposed that they turn it into a six-man match.

The match got started with less than 10 minutes left in the show, and it went right into a commercial break, so we knew we wouldn't get much out of this main event.

They had to rush, but they were able to make this feel competitive with a limited amount of time to work. Williams scored the win by pinning Saints with the Book End.

Fenix has somehow made the AAA cruiserweight title the most visible on WWE television, which is ironic when you consider how much trouble WWE has had maintaining a cruiserweight division every time it has tried.

The way WWE has chosen to use the Lucha Bros is strange, but letting them have some singles success has been nice to see.

As of now, WWE is still planning to hold Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia, so a lot of this week's show was spent hyping the PLE.

The title match between Green and Perez was a strong performance, but it was hurt by a lackluster interference ending.

The Street Fight between Monroe and Giulia felt lifeless at times, the women's tag title change seemed random, and the men's tag match being canceled did little to help that feud.

The final match of the night with Zayn. Gargano, Saints, Penta, Williams and Fenix was the best thing on the show, but it wasn't a high bar to clear. Green vs. Perez was better in some aspects, so it may come down to personal preference.

WWE has all of the tools to deliver a great show every week, but it feels like the last couple of episodes have been booked on autopilot. Let's hope things pick up as we get to the end of 2026.

articles.title: Simone Biles reacts after Michelle Obama names her among the greatest athletes in her Mount Rushmore of sports GOATs: "Mrs. Michelle Obama, you..."
articles.summary: Simone Biles received a special compliment from former first lady Michelle Obama, who named the American gymnast among the four women on her personal
articles.body: Simone Biles received a special compliment from former first lady Michelle Obama, who named the American gymnast among the four women on her personal Mount Rushmore of athletes. Biles did not hide her excitement, sharing a heartfelt response on Instagram after Obama praised her achievements and the demands of gymnastics. "Mrs. Michelle Obama, you made my year," Biles wrote. The recognition came during Obama's appearance on the Is She Game? podcast on October 20, 2026, where she discussed her favorite female athletes and explained why Biles belongs among the greatest in sports.Simone Biles responds to Michelle Obama's praiseSimone Biles' response was short, but it showed how much Obama's words meant to her. The 11-time Olympic medalist took to her Instagram Story to thank the former first lady for including her among the athletes she admires most.Being praised for winning medals is one thing. Receiving recognition from someone who has spent years supporting women's sports and celebrating athletes carries a different kind of meaning. Obama did not simply mention Biles as a champion. She spoke about the physical demands, preparation and mental strength required to compete in gymnastics.Her words clearly struck a chord with Biles, who has built a career on performances that push the limits of the sport. The gymnast's response also gave fans a glimpse of the person behind the medals: even an athlete with her record can be moved by recognition from someone she respects.Michelle Obama explains why Biles belongs among the greatsDuring the podcast appearance, Obama spoke about her admiration for gymnastics and the level of athletic ability it requires. She praised Biles' range of skills, saying, "She can do it all."Obama also pointed to the training and conditioning that often go unnoticed when people watch gymnasts compete. She questioned whether the sport receives enough credit for the physical demands placed on its athletes, particularly when they perform difficult skills under pressure.Biles' ability to generate height during her floor routine caught Obama's attention, too. She wondered whether the gymnast could rise around 13 feet into the air. Biles is 4 feet, 8 inches tall and can reach roughly 12 feet off the ground during her floor exercise, according to the report.Obama also recognised the risks gymnasts take to perform at the highest level. "To know what they were going through and still performing at that risk level, and conquering it."She summed up her view with another clear endorsement: "I think that a Simone Biles has to be a G.O.A.T. I say that for all gymnasts."Serena Williams, Billie Jean King and Lisa Leslie complete the listBiles was one of four women Obama selected for her hypothetical Mount Rushmore of athletes. Her choices also included tennis greats Serena Williams and Billie Jean King, along with basketball legend Lisa Leslie.The selection brought together athletes from different sports and generations. Williams' achievements in tennis made her an obvious figure to recognise, while King earned praise not only for her sporting success but also for her character. Obama described King as a "beautiful human being."Leslie filled the basketball spot. Obama called her a "groundbreaking woman of my era," recognising her place in the growth of women's basketball.The list was not presented as an official ranking. Instead, it reflected the athletes Obama believes have made lasting contributions to women's sports through their ability, influence and example. For Biles, the distinction came with a personal message that needed only seven words to make its impact: "Mrs. Michelle Obama, you made my year."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Para Games 2026: India wins record 114 medals with just 168 athletes
articles.summary: A smaller Indian contingent has delivered a bigger return, rewriting the nation’s Asian Para Games record with 114 medals in Nagoya.
articles.body: A smaller Indian contingent has delivered a bigger return, rewriting the nation’s Asian Para Games record with 114 medals in Nagoya. India’s haul of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze is its best-ever at the continental event, with para-athletics the engine of a campaign that exceeded expectations.Only 168 Indian athletes — 112 men, 56 women — competed across 11 sports, little more than half the 303 sent to Hangzhou in 2023. Yet India has surpassed its previous best of 111 medals there, when it finished fifth and bettered the 72-medal return from Jakarta in 2018, where 190 athletes represented the country.Track and field athletes were the standout, collecting 65 medals, including 22 gold. Para-badminton was next biggest contributor with 16, meaning the two events combined for 81 medals — more than 70 percent of India’s tally. The numbers underline how effectively a squad converted opportunity into podium finishes.Friday brought a flourish, with India winning nine gold medals — its best singleday gold haul of these Games. Sandeep stormed to the men’s 400m T64 title in a world-record 52.28s, while Haney won the men’s javelin F37/38 gold with a worldrecord throw of 60.49m.Sumit Antil, the Paralympic champion, defended his javelin crown in the men’s F42-44/61-64 combined event with a throw of 72.46m. It was not a record, but enough to lead an Indian sweep: Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar bronze with 64.48m.Pranav Soorma defended his men’s club throw F51 title with a Games-record 32.87m. Sandeep’s compatriot Ajay Kumar claimed bronze in 400m T64 in a Games-record 53.61s. Nimisha C won silver in women’s long jump T47 with 5.37m, while Parmod Bijarnia took silver in the men’s 1500m T46 in 4:09.65.India stood fourth on Friday, ahead of South Korea, which has 28 gold, 36 silver and 33 bronze (97). With finals scheduled for Saturday and no Indian entries in those events, the ranking remained vulnerable: three Korean gold would take them to 31 and move them ahead. Even two would level the gold count at 30, with Korea’s silver advantage deciding the tie-break.Whatever the final order, India’s record haul has made this a landmark campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: No. 1 New Canaan football runs past No. 2 Greenwich and extends winning streak to 29
articles.summary: New Canaan and Greenwich have met in a 1 vs. 2 battle in each of the past two years, with the Rams winning each time.
articles.body:
GREENWICH - New Canaan used a ground-and-pound offense to score on its first two possessions of the second half and defeated Greenwich 23-19 in a showdown of the top two teams in the GametimeCT Top 10 Poll Friday night at Cardinal Stadium.

Dallas George capped a 54-yard drive with a 14-yard touchdown run to give the Rams the lead in the third quarter, and Jack Crowell scored on a four-yard run to extend the advantage to 10 points in the fourth quarter.

New Canaan, which has been ranked No. 1 in the GametimeCT poll since the preseason, pushed its state-best winning streak to 29 games, while second-ranked Greenwich fell to 5-1.

It's the second straight season in which the Rams and Cardinals have clashed as the top-ranked teams in the state. New Canaan won last year's game 14-7 at Dunning Field, forcing turnovers on the final two Greenwich drives.

Both teams went on to win state championships. New Canaan has won four straight in Class L and Greenwich has won two straight in Class LL .

Friday's game was also the 10th meeting between the No. 1 and No. 2 teams in the GametimeCT Top 10 poll since 2005, and coming in, the second-ranked teams had a 5-4 advantage.

New Canaan leads the overall series against Greenwich at 23-16-3, and beat the Cardinals 14-7 in both 2021 and 2025. Greenwich's last win was 35-0 in the 2018 Class LL final.

Both teams are kicking off a difficult stretch of games.

New Canaan hosts No. 6 Ludlowe (5-0) in Week 8, followed by No. 2 (tie) St. Joseph (5-0), Wilton (3-3) and Darien (2-3), while Greenwich plays at Ridgefield (3-2) in Week 8, with Wilton, St. Joseph and Staples (5-1) to follow.

articles.title: Danny Sprinkle Addresses Washington Huskies Payroll Situation
articles.summary: The Huskies men's basketball coach was honest about the team's limitations in spending.
articles.body:
SEATTLE — The Washington Huskies men's basketball team was tasked with replacing three-fifths of the roster this offseason. And it had much more limited resources to do so than previous years under head coach Danny Sprinkle.

It was reported by CBS Sports earlier this week that the Huskies were among the lowest spenders among Power Four men's basketball programs ($5-7 million) and the lowest spender in the Big Ten.

"There's some factors that limit us," UW head coach Danny Sprinkle said in a news conference Tuesday at Alaska Airlines Arena. "But, I said it last year, Illinois doesn't care that we're limited. Michigan — nobody cares. We're in the Big Ten, we have to find a way. And we're committed to finding a way and we're committed to doing it the right way. Getting these guys and getting them better. Getting our players better, helping them become better people, better students, better everywhere. And then, at the end of the day, if we're doing that, hopefully those wins come along with it."

Sprinkle isn't using the financial side of things as an excuse for lack of results. In his previous two seasons as head coach, the team is 29-35 overall and 11-29 against Big Ten competition.

However, the lack of funds has had a noticeable impact on recruiting. The team had two international commitments from this past offseason (Wini Braga — Brazil; Tristan Devers — Australia) and has players from five different countries on the roster. Eight of the 15 players on the roster are in their third year of college ball or later. That number includes several transfer portal additions, including fifth-year wing LeJuan Watts (transferred from Texas Tech ) and fourth-year point guard Ryan Beasley (transferred from San Francisco).

"It's hard," Fisch said. "But like I said, our athletic department, we're fighting every day. We are. Our athletic department, we're fighting every day to help these kids get paid more and to get out and find companies locally to help with (Name, Image and Likeness deals). Literally working their tail off. The coaches, everybody here from soccer to track to football, women's basketball. We are all doing everything we can. ... Making the jump to the Big Ten, and I think our fans are figuring this out, it's a lot harder than we thought. It's not the Pac-12. From a travel standpoint, from the teams we play — I'm just speaking for men's basketball — it's completely different."

It'll be a tough task for Sprinkle and the rest of the team to remain competitive year-over-year against the better-funded teams in the Big Ten, but the team has no choice but to try.

The first step for Sprinkle and UW to reach that goal is to post a winning overall and conference season. The 2026-27 campaign will begin against the Colgate Red Raiders at 7 p.m. PT on Nov. 2 at Alaska Airlines Arena in Seattle.

articles.body: India’s young squash star Anahat Singh saw her run at the Silicon Valley Open come to an end after losing 3-1 to Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam on Friday (local time) in Redwood City.The 18-year-old started strongly, winning the opening game 11-5. However, Sivasangari bounced back to take the next three games 11-6, 11-4 and 11-7, securing a 3-1 victory and a place in the final.The Malaysian had also beaten Anahat in the women’s singles final at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, denying the Indian a gold medal.Sivasangari praises Anahat’s talentAfter the match, Sivasangari praised Anahat’s skills and said the young Indian was already among the leading players despite her age. She explained that finding her accuracy helped her recover after a slow start and take control of the contest.“Anahat is very talented and so dangerous. articles.title: Brookhaven football defense dominates in big win over South Jones
articles.summary: Brookhaven's defense shuts down South Jones in the Panthers' 49-16 win on Oct. 23.
articles.body:
The Brookhaven defense made its presence felt all night long in the Panthers' 49-16 win over South Jones.

In the first quarter of the game on Oct. 23 at South Jones High School, Brookhaven (8-0) scored two defensive touchdowns, sucking the energy out of the home crowd and helping the the Panthers jump out to an early 28-0 lead.

The unit is typically led by senior defensive lineman and University of Texas commit Derwin Fields, and while Fields had an impactful night in the trenches, the defensive standouts for Brookhaven were sophomore defensive end Landon Baker and senior defensive back Reece McNulty, both of whom returned interceptions for touchdowns in the first quarter.

"It just made me happy," Fields said. "It's just great seeing them on the field doing what they got to do and executing the job."

The fast start set the tone for the rest of the game and quickly killed any upset aspirations that South Jones (6-3) had. In the second quarter, safety Semaj Ross intercepted a pass for the defense's third of the first half.

"I was very pleased with how we came out in the beginning," Brookhaven coach Darien Dorsey said. "We were locked in. We matched the energy that they brought to the game."

Fields' night was not flashy, but South Jones' offense continued to run the ball away from him throughout the game. Still, Fields recorded three tackles for loss and a quarterback hit.

"Once I figured out that they were trying to run the ball away from me, I was just trying to do my job so everybody else could step in and make the play," Fields said.

In the second half, Brookhaven's defense continued to shut down South Jones, allowing just three points in the final two quarters. In three games this month, Brookhaven's opponents are averaging 9.67 points per game.

On the other side of the ball, the Panthers dominated on the ground. Junior Adrian Blakely and seniors Jordyn Kees and A'Semiyon Smith combined for five rushing touchdowns, but Blakely led the way with three.

"We've got a great running back room," Dorsey said. "We've got three guys that, in any given moment, we can give them the ball. And the offensive line did a phenomenal job of getting them lanes to run in."

Brookhaven returns to action next week against North Pike, looking to stay perfect on the season, but Dorsey and the Panthers are not focused on their undefeated record.

"One game at a time," Dorsey said. "I always tell them that each school that we play have our names circled on that schedule, so they're going to bring out their best. We've got to be able to meet that challenge."

articles.title: Celtics HC Joe Mazzulla gives defensive props to Jayson Tatum, Jordan Walsh after win over Knicks
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics bounced back from their season opener loss to take down the nba champ New York Knicks on Friday. The 107-103 loss of Boston left head coac...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics bounced back from their season opener loss to take down the nba champ New York Knicks on Friday. The 107-103 loss of Boston left head coach Joe Mazzulla impressed and he made sure to praise Jayson Tatum, Jordan Walsh for their defensive showing during the game.

Mazzulla appeared relaxed during his postgame press conference after the Celtics secured their first victory of the season. He highlighted Tatum's ability to make an impact beyond scoring .

"You look at the stat sheet tonight, 14-for-26, 36 points, that's probably the game that everybody expects 82 nights a year," Mazzulla said. "I'll be a betting man that he gets something similar to that most nights. But his greatness has to be in other ways for us. He takes on the challenge of being disruptive defensively."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Walsh' determination to accept the challenge of defending Jalen Brunson also received a nod from Mazzulla.

"You know they took the challenge, and it's not easy," he said. "I thought tonight you saw a version of like at his best. That's what he's going to be for us, and he's going to continue to get better.

Tatum finished as the game's leading scorer with 36 points , nine rebounds and seven assists, converting 14 of his 26 field-goal attempts. The performance also marked the 200th game of his career in which he scored at least 30 points. Meanwhile, Walsh recorded five points and grabbed three rebounds.

Paul George and Neemias Queta also made valuable contributions to Boston's win, scoring 15 points each. Derrick White added 12 points and dished out six assists.

New York entered the game hoping to bounce back from its season-opening loss to the Philadelphia 76ers. However, the defending champions dropped to 0-2 after failing to contain Boston during the crucial moments of the game.

The Celtics will return home to take on the Chicago Bulls on Monday, while the Knicks are set to face the Orlando Magic on Sunday.

articles.title: Denver Nuggets Announce Cam Johnson Injury Status vs. New Orleans Pelicans
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets faced the Oklahoma City Thunder on Thursday to open their season.After a hot first quarter, the Nuggets struggled to shoot the ball for th...
articles.body:
The Denver Nuggets faced the Oklahoma City Thunder on Thursday to open their season.

After a hot first quarter, the Nuggets struggled to shoot the ball for the rest of the game as they suffered a 96-84 loss.

To make matters worse, Cam Johnson suffered an ankle injury late in the second quarter after contesting Ajay Mitchell's shot.

Johnson finished the game with five points and two rebounds in 11 minutes.

Denver Nuggets Announce Cam Johnson Injury Status

According to the Denver Nuggets' injury report for Saturday's game against the New Orleans Pelicans, Cam Johnson is out with a sprained right ankle.

Johnson will miss his first game of the season, which means DeMar DeRozan could enter the starting lineup.

DeRozan earned the bulk of minutes following Johnson's exit. He had 13 points and five rebounds in 28 minutes.

Alpha Diallo could also be named starter since DeRozan might be better suited as a source of instant offense off the bench.

It has been a rough time for Johnson in Denver. He was initially acquired from the Brooklyn Nets in exchange for Michael Porter Jr. and a 2032 first-round pick.

Johnson played in just 54 games in his first season in Denver due to multiple injuries. He had a minor bicep injury early in the campaign, followed by a bone bruise and a hyperextended right knee. He also dealt with ankle issues late in the regular season.

Cam Johnson isn't the only player on the Denver Nuggets injury report.

Alpha Diallo is listed as questionable due to a sprained right wrist. He could get downgraded to out or upgraded to available before the start of Saturday's matchup.

Spencer Jones has also been ruled out for the second straight game as the team continues to manage his bilateral hamstring injury. Jones can be considered day-to-day moving forward.

Julian Strawther remains sidelined as he recovers from a sprained left knee suffered in the preseason. Strawther is scheduled to get re-evaluated in late November.

The Nuggets have endured injuries since last season, which means it's the next-man-up mentality for coach David Adelman's team.

Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray are also coming off a bad first game, so they are looking to bounce back. Aaron Gordon was phenomenal against the Oklahoma City Thunder and looked healthy after missing 49 games last season.

articles.summary: The Winnipeg Jets have put an end to the Connor Hellebuyck trade saga. Winnipeg has traded the former MVP to the New Jersey Devils. In return, the Jets rec...
articles.body:
The Winnipeg Jets have put an end to the Connor Hellebuyck trade saga. Winnipeg has traded the former MVP to the New Jersey Devils . In return, the Jets received four players and two draft picks.

Winnipeg acquired forwards Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, and Alexander Command; goalie Nico Daws; and the aforementioned draft picks. For the first time since 2015-16, the Jets do not have Hellebuyck on their roster. For general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff, he is fine with how things turned out .

"I'm very comfortable (with) what we accomplished here over the period of time," Cheveldayoff said, via NHL.com. "I certainly wish we could have done it four months ago, or whatever, when the opportunity started and we were looking (for a trade), but here we are here today."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Hellebuyck is the best goaltender of this generation. He is one of eight goaltenders to ever win the Hart Trophy as league MVP. He is also one of three goalies to win it after the turn of the century.

However, the Jets largely never truly contended for a Stanley Cup. They made one Western Conference Finals appearance during his time in Winnipeg. But that ended in a four-game sweep at the hands of the Vegas Golden Knights in 2018.

Hellebuyck has a chance to compete for a Stanley Cup in New Jersey. Meanwhile, the Jets can now focus entirely on hockey. Stuart Skinner is the undisputed starter, and this is his crease. It will be interesting to see how all parties are affected by this trade moving forward.

The Jets are in action again on October 25 against the Montreal Canadiens in the Heritage Classic.

articles.summary: The Duke Blue Devils found themselves down to the Virginia Cavaliers late in the fourth quarter of their ACC clash on Friday. The Cavaliers were up 13-7 at h...
articles.body:
The Duke Blue Devils found themselves down to the Virginia Cavaliers late in the fourth quarter of their ACC clash on Friday. The Cavaliers were up 13-7 at halftime, but while Duke tied the game 13-13 in the fourth, Virginia went ahead 16-13 with a field goal of their own with less than two minutes left in the game.

But just like he has for much of this season, running back Nate Sheppard came to Duke's rescue. He did not get a touchdown with his feet, though; instead, he used his arm in a sneaky double-pass trick play .

After receiving a backward pass from quarterback Walker Eget, Sheppard uncorked a pass to wide receiver Brody Keefe, who was wide open for the touchdown.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Virginia still had a chance to tie after Duke missed the point after kick, which kept the score at 19-16. However, the Cavaliers' comeback hopes were dashed after quarterback Beau Pribula's pass on fourth down was intercepted by the Duke defense.

Sheppard, who had been dealing with an undisclosed injury , has been outstanding for Duke in both the running and receiving game this season. Heading into the game, he had 820 rushing yards with eight touchdowns, to go with 28 catches for 259 yards over six games. He was also coming off back-to-back games of 170 or more yards from scrimmage. He was limited to just 66 yards from scrimmage against Virginia, but he made up for it with the game-winning touchdown throw.

With the win, Duke improved to 5-2 on the season, while Virginia dropped to 4-4. The Blue Devils will look to clinch bowl eligibility on Halloween, when they host Boston College in Durham.

articles.title: Vikings-Colts Final Injury Report
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Indianapolis Colts released their final injury reports along with injury designations in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings and Indianapolis Colts released their final injury reports along with injury designations in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at U.S. Bank Stadium. Here they are.

PUP = Physically unable to participate list.

IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed.

Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day.

Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day.

Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day.

Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing.

For the Vikings, only Jordan Mason has an injury designation, but his questionable designation is a technical one for those coming off of IR. He will play on Sunday. Christian Darrisaw and Harrison Smith had their customary rest days on Friday.

For the Colts, a total of seven players have injury designations. The most significant are starting cornerback Sauce Gardner and starting tight end Tyler Warren, both of whom are out, as is wide receiver Anthony Gould.

Starting linebacker Bryce Boettcher is questionable, as is his backup C.J. Allen, which could leave them thin at the position. The same is true at cornerback with Sauce Gardner out and Justin Walley questionable.

Lastly, punter Rigoberto Sanchez did not practice all week and is listed as questionable. The Colts added a punter to their roster this week in case he can't go on Sunday.

So there you have it. Inactive players will be listed about an hour before game time.

articles.title: With 'complete performance,' Milton football stuns Franklin in rout
articles.summary: Franklin came into Milton riding high Friday night, October 23. The Panthers left the South Shore with a humbling defeat.
articles.body:
MILTON — With the arm of Sean Lane and the hands of Taj Chung, the Milton High football team delivered its best performance of the season.

The senior quarterback led the way, completing 11 of 16 passes for 139 yards and four touchdowns and Chung hauled in four receptions for 72 yards and three scores as the Wildcats declawed heavily favored Franklin en route to a convincing 41-6 victory in Friday night's highly anticipated non-league match-up at a packed Brooks Stadium at Milton High School.

The Wildcats, who were seeded eighth in the MIAA Division 3 power rankings, aimed to reverse the course following last week's 21-0 shutout loss to Walpole.

Other contributors for the Wildcats included Jayden DuBois, who rushed for 90 yards on 11 carries and a touchdown while senior tri-captain Peter Skutnik added 74 yards on 11 rushes and a score.

"It's a great win for us, and it's our most complete performance of the season,'' said Wildcat coach Steve Dembowski, whose squad improves to 5-2 overall. "Last week against (Walpole), we laid an egg (21-0) loss, and we needed to find a way to redeem ourselves. This is a great win for our seeding, as the regular season is winding down and we want to avoid falling into that 7-10 bracket. This is a huge win,, and it definitely gives us momentum heading into the (Division 3) post-season."

On a 13-play game-opening scoring drive that spanned 61-yards, the Wildcats drew first blood and emerged with a 6-0 lead. After a pair of rushes by Peter Skutnik, quarterback Sean Lane managed a pair of rushes to drive into Panther territory.

After a six-yard rush by Jayden DuBois, Lane fired a completed pass into the slot for a 15-yard gain to the Panther 12. On a third and five from the six, the Wildcats capped the scoring drive as Lane spotted receiver Peter Mullen wide open in the back of the end zone with 5:35 remaining in the first quarter en route to the 6-0 lead.

"I thought we were able to really establish control of the game in that first drive,'' said Dembowski. "We were able to convert a few third down plays, and we were able to get out in front early.:

Only 1:57 later, the Panthers tied the contest at 6-6, retaliating on a quick four play drive that mustered 63 yards. On the first play from scrimmage, sophomore Ethan Edmunds, who completed just six of 20 passes for 100 yards, fired a 39-yard strike to Christian Holmes. After a pair or rushes by Owen Essam and Edmunds, Holmes broke through several tacklers at the line of scrimmage and dashed into the end zone with 3:55 remaining, Following a missed extra-point attempt, both teams were mired in a 6-6 tie before the Wildcats capitalized on three drives for 21 unanswered points in cruising to 27-6 halftime edge.

"They (Franklin) came back, and scored on their first drive, and at first, it looked like it was going to be a track meet,'' said Dembowski. "After (Franklin) scored, we regained our composure, and I thought we really executed well in all three phases of the game. We controlled the line of scrimmage, and we were able to spread the ball around. We had a lot of guys, who really contributed and it was a total team win.

After both teams traded possessions, the Wildcats capitalized on a 19-yard punt by the Panthers and quickly regained the lead at 13-6.. On a first down from the Panther 32, Lane fired a 26-yard strike to Chung. Moments later, Lane connected with Dylan Raffle on a six-yard touchdown pass with 2:03 remaining in the first quarter followed by Lane's successful extra-point attempt.

Aiming to strike back, the Panthers failed to execute on a seven play drive that spanned 42-yards, Driving to the Wildcat 42-yard line, the Panthers were faced with a fourth and 8, but failed to capitalize as Edmunds scrambled for just one yard as the Wildcats once again were handed favorable field position.

"They (Milton) weren't giving us any different looks,'' said Panthers coach Todd Kiley. "It's the same stuff that we practiced all week. We've just got to protect (Edmunds) a little better. He (Edmunds) was flushed out a bunch, so we've got to take a look at where things broke down. "They (Milton) have an exceptionally talented squad. Seeing them suffer a 21-0 defeat last week came as a real shock, since their game tape clearly demonstrates how formidable they are."

Capitalizing on the short field, the Wildcats struck again with a quick two play 59-yard scoring drive. After Lane fired a 39-yard strike downfield to senior tri-captain tight end Jack Kelly, Skutnik followed through, breaking through several tackles at the line of scrimmage and blitzed into the end zone with 5:58 remaining in the first half for the 20-6 lead.

Faced with a fourth and two from the Wildcat 37, the Panthers elected to gamble as Edmunds was stopped just inches short of the first down marker on a failed quarterback draw.

Just two plays later, the Wildcats capitalized and increased the lead to 27-6 as DuBois broke through several tackles at the line of scrimmage and dashed into the end zone for the 35-yard score with 2:52 remaining in the first half.

"Not being able to convert on fourth downs and giving them the short fields, that hurt,'' said Kiley. "But that's us. We're going to be aggressive. I will never change that for as long as I coach. That's who we are. We believe in our kids, we believe they can make those plays. Give credit to Milton. They made those plays. We didn't."

With a 21-point lead in hand at the half, the Wildcats continued to add to the scoring early in the third quarter. Working again with the short field, the Wildcats responded with a seven play 37-yard scoring drive that was finished with Lane's third touchdown pass of the contest. On a fourth down from the Panther 10, Lane fired a fade to Chung in the deep corner of the end zone with 7:26 remaining for the 34-6 lead.

"I've played against Todd (Kiley) several times,'' said Dembowski, whose teams also went against Kiley when he coached Holliston. "They (Franklin) do a great job coaching. I just thought our kids really responded. We needed a performance like this, and the guys knew that. I thought our coaches had a good game plan, and at the line of scrimmage we dominated on both sides.Todd plays the full 48 minutes. You want to be able to control the second half and not have any letdown at the end of the game, no matter what the score."

Capping the scoring, the Wildcats finished a nine-play, 58-yard scoring drive. On a second and 10 from the Panther 17, Lane scrambled to his right and connected on a wide open Chung for his fourth touchdown pass of the night with 1:22 remaining in the third quarter as the Wildcats eased to the win.

"I just told the team, hey, it's one game,'' said Kiley. "Everybody has one of these. We had ours this week."

articles.title: Hillsdale throttles Chippewa in Week 10, clinches share of WCAL title
articles.summary: The Falcons knew a win in Week 10 would clinch their first league championship since 2014. They made a statement early and never looked back.
articles.body:
DOYLESTOWN - Kael Lewis has started in back-to-back state championship games .

He holds every passing record known to man at Hillsdale, his class is the winningest in program history, he is a three-sport All-Ohioan and was twice named first team on the gridiron already.

But one thing has always eluded him — a league championship.

Hillsdale's dominant 41-0 win over Chippewa in Week 10 was the 44th in these seniors' careers and arguably the sweetest as it clinched a share of the Wayne County Athletic League title, the Falcons' first since 2014.

"It means everything, this is what you work for all season," Lewis said. "We fell short the last two years at 9-0 then losing the league title game — those hurt more than anything — but it's all worth this feeling right now."

The impressive win over rival Norwayne last week brought the Falcons into a three-way tie with the Bobcats and Smithville heading into the regular season finale. A win over the Chipps was all Hillsdale needed to end the 12-year drought, and the team wanted to make a statement early.

"They started off strong against Norwayne and Smithville," Lewis said of Chippewa. "So we knew if we got off to a good start then it would be too for our defense. And they played lights out tonight giving us great field position to go down and score."

Defense forced a three-and-out for the Chipps on their opening drive, and the offense wasted no time as Lewis hit Ayden Salyer from 28 yards for the team's first of six touchdowns on the night. Porter Boreman rushed in from 9 yards out on the next possession and a Knox Lewis interception in Chippewa territory set up Boreman's second for a 20-0 lead after one.

A quick second quarter saw Chippewa drive down to the Hillsdale 9-yard line before Brock Bennett threw an interception to Reed Mager in the end zone with 28 seconds to go in the half. Starting at the 20, Lewis scrambled three times for 40 yards to get to the Chippewa 40-yard line with five seconds remaining. And on the final play of the half he dropped back, patiently waited for his receivers to get near the end zone, then heaved one downfield to Davis Radcliffe who made a contested grab for the score.

"We weren't even gonna go for it, we were just gonna kneel and go (to halftime)," Lewis said with a laugh. "But we had two timeouts and a dream Hail Mary ... we have a bunch of guys over 6 feet as receivers which many teams don't have, just throw it up and we'll come down with it."

Lewis connected with Salyer again early in the third quarter from 23 yards out — another highlight reel catch for the Falcons — to bring the running clock into effect before Mager capped off the night with a 2-yard scamper.

"I trust those guys," Lewis said of his receivers. "I've been blessed with some really good receivers the last few years, and I trust those guys more than anything. Ayden Salyer, just throw it up to him, there's no 50-50 ball in his vocab."

He finished 8-of-10 for 139 yards and three touchdowns and added another 57 yards on eight carries. Salyer had four receptions for 83 yards and two scores, Radcliffe two catches for 48 yards and a score plus 44 yards on the ground on four carries.

"It says a lot about this group," Hillsdale coach Trevor Cline said. "This championship is not only for them, but all those groups that came before then. It has been really cool in recent years how supportive the alumni have been ... some of the guys who maybe weren't as fortunate or part of the teams that were successful are some of our biggest fans. And that's what it's all about ... even though you graduate, you're still part of the program. The last two years we had some really good teams and for whatever reason it just didn't work out where we were able to get a league championship.

"For this group to do that when they were doubted from the get-go — when you lose 15 seniors, that's a steep hill to climb — but our guys throughout the entire offseason showed up and worked hard. No matter what anyone said on the outside, we just kept finding ways to keep getting better. When you do that and put the team before self, you can accomplish special things."

It was Cline's third league title having won twice as a quarterback for the Falcons in 2010 and 2011.

"It's extremely special whenever you can achieve a championship," Cline said. "It doesn't matter if it's a league championship, regional championship — one day our goal is to win a state championship, too — it's just cool because you know the amount of time that goes into this stuff. Not only as coaches, but the players, too. To do it with this group of just five seniors — we're a fairly young team — for them to achieve a championship is neat."

And this dominant run to close out the regular season was all sparked by the loss to Smithville in Week 5 .

"I was really upset," Lewis said. "I wanted to be the first Hillsdale team to go 10-0 because I knew what we were capable of. That hurt really bad, but we knew that a league title (was still possible). We knew Norwayne was good enough to upset Smithville and that's exactly what happened."

Over the final five weeks the Falcons outscored opponents 219-17 with a pair of shutouts and no more than one score allowed by any team.

"Our defense has played really well throughout the entire year, credit coach (Josh) Barr and coach (Michael) Mack on that side of the ball," Cline said. "They've done a really nice job with our defense this year, and in previous years ... the buy-in from 11 guys — and even more than that because we have guys subbing in a good amount — they just love to hit and get after it on the defensive end, and they've been extremely disciplined.

"In the Smithville game we had a few lapses and they caught us on some plays — just us not being disciplined. But since that game they've used it as motivation, and if you could see our guys in practice, you wouldn't be surprised about why they've gotten better each week. We have an extremely focused group this year and a group that wants to find ways to get better every day. We challenge every team at the beginning of the year to find ways to get better so by the end of the year, we're a heck of a lot better.

"This group did a great job accomplishing that."

And they're hoping to accomplish more. Hillsdale clinched a first-round bye in the playoffs as the three-seed in Division VI, Region 21. The Falcons will await their opponent for Week 12 and get a chance to rest up and recovery from the grueling regular season.

"I feel really confident," Lewis said. "We know Region 21 is a gauntlet this year with South Range (9-1), Smithville (8-2), and Kirtland (9-1), but I think we're right up there with those guys.

"This is the most laser focused I've ever been with this team. In practices, every rep means something and we know what we're working towards ... we're getting better every week, and I trust us against anyone."

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Mona Agarwal smashes WR for 2nd gold
articles.summary: Mona Agarwal shattered a world record to clinch her second gold medal, while archers Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi teamed up for the top prize in the
articles.body: Mona Agarwal shattered a world record to clinch her second gold medal, while archers Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi teamed up for the top prize in the men’s para recurve doubles as India enjoyed another fine day at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya on Friday.Mona stole the spotlight, clinching her second gold of the Games with a WR score of 357.5 in the women’s 50m rifle three positions SH1 final. She finished 3.8 points ahead of China’s Cuiping Zhang, who settled for silver, while compatriot Avani Lekhara finished fourth.The 38-year-old had opened her campaign with gold in the women’s 10m air rifle standing SH1 event, setting a Games record. Her double-gold haul underlined her consistency and composure on the shooting range.Indian para shooters wrapped up their campaign with five medals — two gold, two silver and one bronze — providing a significant boost to the country’s overall tally.On the archery field, Harvinder and Sundi combined brilliantly to beat China 5-1 in the men’s para recurve doubles final. After sharing the opening set, the Indian duo won the next two to seal the title.Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan added silver in the women’s recurve doubles after losing 0-6 to China. Harvinder and Bhawna narrowly missed bronze in the mixed team event, going down to Iran in a shoot-off.Para archery ended with six medals, including three gold and three silver, capping a strong campaign.Mona, Nishad to lead Indian contingent at closing ceremonyDouble gold medallists Mona and high jumper Nishad Kumar have been named India’s flagbearers for Saturday’s closing ceremony. Nishad won gold in the men’s high jump and long jump T47 events, joining Mona among the standout performers of India’s campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fans react to Brewers 'winning twice' after chaotic ninth inning call
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers thought they'd beaten the Tampa Bay Rays, but a challenge overturned the call and extended the game. The Crew still got it done.
articles.body:
Don't feel bad if you prematurely thought the Milwaukee Brewers won their first World Series game in 44 years.

Both Jacob Misiorowski and Christian Yelich assumed the same. As did the second base umpire, Fox Sports play-by-play broadcaster Joe Davis, and apparently whoever controls the post-win fireworks. Probably everyone tuned into the broadcast did, too.

They all assumed shortstop Cooper Pratt caught the ball with his foot still on second base and he turned a double-play to secure a 4-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays and take a 1-0 series lead.

They were all wrong. So don't beat yourself up if you were, too.

Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays highlights, World Series Game 1

It took a challenge from Rays manager Kevin Cash and a replay review to make that clear. But, it was. With one out in the bottom of the ninth inning, Tampa Bay mounting a comeback and Milwaukee closer Trevor Megill under pressure to secure a victory, what appeared at first glance to be a game-winning double play was not.

As Rays star Junior Caminero ran towards second base, Brewers second baseman Brice Turang threw to Pratt. Pratt stood on the bag when the throw left Turang's hand, but took it off too early and Caminero was safe at second.
