articles.title: Pennsylvania high school football coach dies after in-game medical emergency
articles.summary: Cornell High School football coach Ed Dawson died Friday after suffering a medical emergency during a game in Pennsylvania, leaving his community mourning.
articles.body:
Cornell High School (Coraopolis, PA) football coach Ed Dawson died on Friday, Oct. 23, after suffering a "medical emergency" during its Week 9 game against Rochester.

Dawson suffered the medical emergency and died after being transported to a local hospital, according to the Beaver County Times — part of the USA TODAY Network.

He was named the head coach for the Raiders in 2011 and posted a 49-54 record across 12 seasons leading Cornell. During his tenure, Dawson led the Raiders through a co-op and eventually fielded enough players to field its own program in 2016.

Dawson led the team to its first conference championship in 36 years and into the WPIAL semifinals in 2019. Two years later, the program went 7-2 and won its first outright conference title.

"I am extremely saddened and shocked to report that Coach Dawson has passed away," Cornell School District Superintendent Aaron Thomas said in a statement to WTAE .

Coraopolis Mayor Michael Dixon statement

Coraopolis Mayor Michael Dixon issued a statement on Facebook :

"Tonight our community lost one of its giants. Coach Ed Dawson passed away this evening, and the Borough of Coraopolis joins Cornell School District, his players, and his family in heartbreak," Dixon wrote. "When Cornell stepped away from football in 2012, a lot of people assumed Friday nights here were over. Coach Dawson didn't accept that. When the Raiders returned in 2016, he started with a few dozen kids and a lot of faith.

"They lost their first 18 games and kept showing up anyway, even at youth league games, making sure every young person in this town knew there was a place for them on his team. By 2019, he had led the Raiders to their first section title in 36 years, the first WPIAL playoff win in school history, and the WPIAL semifinals. He took them back to the semifinals in 2021.

The wins mattered. The young men he shaped mattered more. Coach Dawson looked for the positive in every game and in every kid, and he taught them to sweat the details and never quit. Generations of Cornell and Nazareth Prep players grew into better men because he believed in them before they believed in themselves.

To Coach Dawson's family: Coraopolis grieves with you, and we will stand beside you in the days ahead. To his players and coaching staff: lean on each other and on this community. You were his team, and you are ours.

Thank you, Coach. We love you, and we will not forget what you built here."

articles.title: Milwaukee fans pack Deer District for Brewers World Series opener
articles.summary: Milwaukee Brewers fans gathered in the Deer District Oct. 23 to celebrate the team's first World Series appearance in 44 years.
articles.body:
With cheers from fans echoing all the way to Dr. M.L.K. Jr. Drive and Juneau Street in Milwaukee, fans gathered in the Deer District Oct. 23 to watch the Milwaukee Brewers ' return to the World Series after 44 years, following the Milwaukee Bucks' home opener.

The day's celebrations began at 3 p.m. with the Bucks' home opener against the Chicago Bulls . The game was originally scheduled for 7 p.m., but the Bucks moved the tip-off time to 3 p.m. on Oct. 16 to accommodate the Brewers' first World Series appearance since 1982.

Despite the Bucks losing their home opener to the Bulls, 132-125, Bucks fans united with Brewers fans ‒ and even a few Bulls fans ‒ outside Fiserv Forum to watch the Brewers take on the Tampa Bay Rays on a giant screen in the middle of the Deer District.

The free outdoor watch party, hosted by Deer District Business Improvement District 53, took place at The Deer Garden.

At least 110 fans gathered around the giant screen, while at least 150 more people opted to watch the game inside the Deer District's bars and restaurants rather than brave the crisp 57-degree weather.

Brewers gear dominated the crowd, with fans sporting jerseys, hats and other team apparel as they gathered to cheer on Milwaukee.

Despite a few technical difficulties with the Jumbotron fading in and out, drawing boos from the crowd, fans continued cheering as they watched a clip of Jacob Misiorowski's now-infamous Pokémon interview , Fox commentators' updated World Series predictions, and Misiorowski stepping up to the mound to throw his historic first pitch , which at 103.5 mph was the fastest-ever pitch thrown in the World Series since pitch tracking began in 2008.

More Brewers World Series watch parties planned in Deer District

The Deer District will continue hosting free outdoor watch parties for the Brewers' upcoming World Series games on Oct. 24, 26 and 27.

Participating bars and restaurants throughout the district offered special promotions during the postseason, including drink specials.

articles.title: Tiago Splitter explains approach to adjusting starting lineups after Bucks win
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls bounced back from a 43-point loss to the Toronto Raptors by defeating the Milwaukee Bucks 132-125. They also made a 15-point comeback. It w...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls bounced back from a 43-point loss to the Toronto Raptors by defeating the Milwaukee Bucks 132-125. They also made a 15-point comeback. It was a case of: it wasn't about how you start, but how you finish.

The starting lineup consisted of Caleb Wilson, Norman Powell, Matas Buzelis, Josh Giddey, and Jalen Smith. In the end, Giddey, Smith, and Buzelis sat on the bench. Instead, Leonard Miller, Tre Jones, and Isaac Okoro played with Wilson and Powell to cap off the game.

After the game, head coach Tiago Splitter explained his decision to use different lineups based on the circumstances, per Will Gottlieb of CHGO_Bulls.

"You've got to see, game-by-game, who's going to finish the game. But you cannot change the starting lineup every time a guy plays well or plays bad. If not, you go crazy; you change every game."

In the end, the changing of the lineups worked out for everyone. Plus, they got the best out of many of those players. Powell finished the game as the leading scorer with 25 points and went 9-for-9 at the free-throw line. Additionally, Caleb Wilson finished with 21 points and 6 rebounds.

Miller came off the bench to add 19 points. Okoro scored 12 points, and Jones added 11 points. Also, Buddy Hield added 13 points. However, Giddey and Buzelis finished with low numbers. Buzelis scored 7 points, and Giddey scored 6. Giddey was listed as probable on the injured list before the game with a left wrist injury.

The Bulls will play the Washington Wizards in their home opener on Saturday.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum vents over Jaylen Brown's 'cap' post as Celtics win overshadowed by trade drama talk
articles.summary: BOSTON (AP) — Jayson Tatum should have been breaking down the nuances of his 36-point performance in Celtics' 107-103 win over the defending champion New Yor...
articles.body:
BOSTON (AP) — Jayson Tatum should have been breaking down the nuances of his 36-point performance in Celtics' 107-103 win over the defending champion New York Knicks.

Instead he spent most of his postgame news conference on Friday night addressing Jaylen Brown's social media response that took issue with Tatum saying in a video on his YouTube channel that he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" by Brown's trade to the Philadelphia 76ers this summer.

Brown responded on his Instagram account with a baseball cap emoji. "Cap" is slang for something that is not true. Asked if he had any response, Tatum sighed before expressing his frustrations with the entire situation for several minutes.

"I don't have any animosity or beef, or ill will towards him. I think the toughest part is since he's not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or the conversations haven't been enough about what we accomplished — all the games we won, winning a championship, how we've grown together. It's turned into this drama type of thing."

Tatum said while he understands there is an entertainment aspect to professional sports and that speculation about their off-court relationship is part of that, he was exasperated with how everything has lingered in recent months.

"I'm not blaming anybody for how they feel," Tatum said. "We all go through different things in our lives. ... People play this game and never got the finals. We did it twice and won a championship. It should be more about that. This ain't no Shaq and Kobe. There's no beef."

Both players have spoken glowingly at times about how they grew and thrived together during their nine years together as teammates.

But it's morphed into something else since the Celtics chose Tatum as the player they want to build around after trading Brown in what amounted to a move to cut one of the two players with $300 million contracts from the payroll.

"It's turned into this drama type of thing," Tatum said. "I've got two kids. I reached out the day he got traded. I called, I texted. And I understand, people process things differently. So, for me at this point in our lives, we are too old to be having our relationship discussed and X, Y and Z on the internet. There's a conversation to be had and we can definitely have that conversation. I welcome that, right?

"I've always wanted the best for him and wished the best for him. I've always publicly said those things."

Tatum also lamented how social media has fueled it.

"I've seen all these things like, 'Get your popcorn ready when they play.' This ain't no (expletive) boxing match. Play basketball. There's no animosity. There's no beef. I just hate the way the conversation and narrative around it inflamed it. There's not enough communication. I think conversation would solve and put out a lot of fires."

Tatum also doesn't believe the conversation — if there is one — would be negative.

"He's just turned 30. I'm 28. I've got two kids. As adults, it's a conversation. I'm not saying it's a bad one or anything like that. Just communication usually gets to right (or) wrong, you'll understand the other side."

articles.title: Feisty Thulasimathi Murugesan turns ‘alien’ tag into medal magic
articles.summary: Called an “alien” and bullied for her dark skin and congenital left-hand deformity, Thulasimathi Murugesan has turned badminton into her most eloquent
articles.body: Called an “alien” and bullied for her dark skin and congenital left-hand deformity, Thulasimathi Murugesan has turned badminton into her most eloquent answer to those who doubted her abilities.On Friday, the 24-year-old produced a golden flourish at Asian Para Games, winning three medals in a single day to spearhead India’s campaign. Thulasimathi and Manasi Joshi clinched women’s doubles SL3-SU5 gold, beating China’s Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13.She added singles SU5 silver after losing to Yang 18-21, 11-21, before partnering Nitesh Kumar to mixed doubles SL3-SU5 silver, losing to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani 21-11, 19-21, 14-21.Born without a thumb on her left hand, Thulasimathi endured restricted movement, financial hardship and relentless teasing. Her daily-wage labourer father, Murugesan, nurtured her sporting ambitions, coaching her with his limited sports knowledge through gruelling routines despite limited resources.From inexpensive shoes and secondhand racquets to international podiums, the Kancheepuram girl’s journey continued. At Paris 2024, she became the first Indian woman to win Paralympic badminton silver, in the women’s singles SU5 category.India finished badminton with 16 medals — three gold, five silver and eight bronze — making it the country’s second-best medal-producing sport after athletics at the Asian Para Games.Nitesh started the gold rush, defeating compatriot Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in men’s singles SL3. Debutant Naveen Sivakumar captured men’s singles SL4 gold, beating Indonesia’s Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17.Bhagat settled for silver, while Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan earned silver in women’s singles SH6 after losing to China’s Li Fengmei 12-21, 13-21.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “LeBron James Hates the Country that Made Him a Billionaire”: Journalist Sounds Off After Golf Swing Practice During National Anthem
articles.summary: LeBron James has started his 76ers career with a bang. Philadelphia beat the defending-champion Knicks, 106-100, in his first game.
articles.body:
LeBron James has started his 76ers career with a bang. Philadelphia beat the defending-champion Knicks, 106-100, in his first game. In his second game, the 76ers beat James' former team, the Cavaliers, 114-106 on Thursday.

He had 14 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists in the first game, and 17 points, 10 rebounds, five assists, and three steals in the second. However, his strong start is the least-discussed part of James' season.

James has faced backlash after he was seen practicing his golf swing during the national anthem on Tuesday. Among others, journalist Clay Travis also presented his negative views on James' actions.

"LeBron would never disrespect the Chinese national anthem like he did the American national anthem this week. LeBron hates the country that made him a billionaire. His brain is broken," Travis captioned his post.

"This is insanely disrespectful. The President was right to call him out for this. He knows all the cameras are gonna be on him. It's not only disrespectful to everyone that has given him this tremendous opportunity but the singer is on the floor right there, singing the national anthem. A highly trained, Grammy winning, Broadway celebrity, who is there putting their heart and soul in that performance. Everyone else on the entire team is able to behave like an adult," Travis said .

President Donald Trump calls out LeBron James

President Trump was fuming after LeBron's actions during the national anthem.

"While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for! President DONALD J. TRUMP," he said on Truth Social.

LeBron brushed off the controversy, calling it a "slow news day," to the reporter who asked for his reply to Trump's comments.

articles.title: Saratoga Springs holds off late rally by Shenendehowa to post a Class AA football win
articles.summary: Saratoga Springs, ranked No. 12 in the state, won its sixth straight/
articles.body:
CLIFTON PARK - When the Saratoga Springs football team got to this stage of the season in 2025, the Blue Streaks traveled to take on Shenendehowa in Week 8 and lost. Friday night, the same two teams met during the same week at the same location. This time around, Saratoga Springs prevailed.

In a hard-hitting tussle between huge rivals carrying playoff implications, the Blue Streaks managed to stave off a late drive by Shen as senior Gavin LaFrance intercepted a pass near the end zone. Two subsequent kneeldowns allowed Saratoga Springs to secure a hardfought 14-10 Class AA victory over the Mustangs at Steuerwald Stadium.

"We knew this would happen. A huge rivalry every year and always a close game. Records really don't mean anything in this game," Saratoga Springs three-year starting quarterback Bobby Morris said. "We knew this one would be a close and we also knew the team with more heart would end up winning the game."

"We knew we were going to see the best version of them," LaFrance said.

Shenendehowa (5-3 overall, 4-3 Class AA), which still landed the final Class AA playoff berth Friday on the strength of Niskayuna's 32-14 win against Albany, led 7-0 in the second quarter and ended up trailing 14-7 at halftime after Morris engineered a pair long touchdown drives.

The lead for Saratoga Springs (7-1, 6-1) was reduced to four points on a 29-yard field goal from Michael Manoli.

"We knew we were going to be get their best - homecoming and they were healthy," Morris said of Shen. "It goes to show that every week you have to show up with the same mindset. You can't look at the records and look at the scores."

Shenendehowa made one late push seeking a go-ahead score, but the 6-foot-3 LaFrance managed to snare a pass by senior quarteback Jack Clawson intended for Deacon Smith just in front of the Blue Streaks' end zone.

"He makes big-time plays in big-time games," Saratoga Springs junior running back and defensive end Cam Toomey said of LaFrance. "That is the type of player he has always been since I have been playing with him."

"They are a special group. Honestly, I think they are the best group I have played with," Morris said of the defense. "You've got my back. They have all of our backs. When we make a mistake on offense, they are right there to pick us back up."

LaFrance is known more for his offensive exploits, yet he managed to make sure his team came away with the victory by producing the night's second interception against Clawson.

"I was about to get over the top to get that pick. There is no better feeling that, coming out on top to help your team win the game," LaFrance said.

On an evening when points were hard to come by, Toomey's relentless pass rush pressure and overall presence at the line of scrimmage helped assure the state's No. 12 ranked Class AA prevailed on the road in a rivalry game. The junior also ran for 85 yards on seven carries.

"The other team has to triple-team him if they don't want him to sack the QB," LaFrance said.

"You just have to have that motor to keep going no matter what," Toomey said. "I have been getting this all season."

173: Passing yards for Clawson on 12-for-25 accuracy. He also rushed for 24 yards on eight attempts.

93: Rushing yards amassed by Morris over 13 carries. The senior also completed 8 of 16 passes for 58 yards.

75: Yards Saratoga's Jaden Lockrow gained over six touches: Four receptions for 39 yards and two carries covering 36 yards. He scored on a 29-yard touchdown run in the second quarter.

The Blue Streaks hit the road for a Week 9 contest Oct. 30 at Guilderland.

The final contest of the regular season has the Mustangs playing at home Oct. 30 vs. Albany.

articles.title: Harrison football wins Sectional 24 opener against Boonville
articles.summary: Harrison football did all of its scoring in the first half en route to a win over Boonville in a Class 4A, Sectional 24 quarterfinal Friday night.
articles.body:
EVANSVILLE — Harrison and Boonville football put on a scoring display to open IHSAA Class 4A, Sectional 24 Friday, Oct. 23. Thirty-four points were put on the board at Romain Stadium in the first half as the Warriors led 20-14.

But in the second half, zero points were scored for either team.

It was not perfect, but the Warriors are moving on to play Bedford North Lawrence (7-3) on the road in the October 30 semifinal. It is Harrison's second sectional win in as many seasons.

Perhaps, a turning point for the program.

"That's one thing that this group can hang their hat on," Harrison coach Moe Sutton said. "I'm happy to get out of here with the win."

Dissatisfaction following a sectional win

As the answer may suggest, Sutton was dissatisfied with what he saw against Boonville. Missed assignments and penalties cost the Warriors at various points of the game.

It was a rough week of practice for Harrison in the lead up to the game, as Sutton said his group had just one good day.

In the team huddle after the game, Sutton told his team he knows they have more in them. He challenged his group; now it is on the Harrison players to show a higher sense of urgency in preparation for the sectional semifinal.

"All the coaches I had growing up will tell you, 'You play like you practice, and you practice like you play,'" Sutton said. "It showed tonight."

Boonville's season is over. After going 4-6 in coach Jonathan Batts' first season, the Pioneers finished with a 6-4 record.

Boonville dealt with injuries to key pieces down the stretch of the season. But the opportunity was there to advance as the game remained close throughout.

"Coming out of the half, our defense played their butts off holding Harrison scoreless," Batts said. "We just struggled when it mattered. Credit coach Sutton and his team, that's a hard-fought ball club right there."

Boonville had its opportunities to score in the second half, but multiple drives were halted in Harrison territory.

In the third quarter, quarterback Beau Seiler threw an interception off a tipped pass that landed in Harrison defensive back Dre Sanders' hands. Later on, Harrison's defense got stops on fourth down to change possession.

Batts was emotional after the game, embracing players as they walked off the field for the last time representing the Pioneers.

The program will continue without a talented senior class of 16 players. That includes key contributors offensively like running back Mason Jones, wide receiver Bradyn Egli and tight end Wyatt Seiler.

"This senior group, man, they mean a lot to me," Batts said. "They fought till the end of that one right there. We came in here shorthanded, but those boys stepped up and they fought."

While they were not the highlight of Sutton's postgame thoughts, Harrison had some positives. The Warriors scored three rushing touchdowns from three different rushers: DK Rankin, Khi'shaun Brown and quarterback Anthony Bavone. Brown's rush was certainly impressive. evading tacklers on his way into the end zone.

Bavone had a good one too, but his most pivotal carry came late in the fourth quarter to give his team the first down that would put the game out of reach.

Harrison has now won four of its last five games. Teams always want to be playing your best football of the season at this point, and the Warriors have been doing just that.

"We're trying to turn it around," Bavone said. "Everybody doubted me at the beginning of the season. What (are) they going to say now?"

Sutton is certain a performance like the one against Boonville will not be enough to defeat Bedford North Lawrence.

"We won, but it wasn't the way I wanted it to look for us," Sutton said. "We'll be here (Saturday) at 8 a.m. as usual and get ready for Bedford."

articles.title: Blake Griffin drops ‘confused’ admission on Chris Paul’s Clippers exit before retirement
articles.summary: The LA Clippers are entering a new era of basketball after having moved on from Kawhi Leonard, James Harden, and Ivica Zubac, but one thing fans still aren’t...
articles.body:
The LA Clippers are entering a new era of basketball after having moved on from Kawhi Leonard, James Harden, and Ivica Zubac, but one thing fans still aren't able to fully get over is the way the franchise moved on from Chris Paul .

Paul and the Clippers parted ways last December, when the franchise elected to send him home after midnight at the start of an East coast road trip. While small reports have come out about what happened, many have continued to wonder what truly was the last straw that broke the camel's back.

On a recent media your, Blake Griffin recently spoke about his former teammate departing from his former team and the franchise that drafted him the way they did.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Yeah, it's disappointing," Griffin said . "I mean, obviously, knowing that that was going to be his last season, you'd think that they knew, you know, what they were getting. And part of what you're getting when you sign a Chris Paul is you're getting his mind. I was just kind of confused at where the disconnect was like, this is who he's been his whole career. He's like a leader, he's a talker. So why not use that to your advantage?"

Blake Griffin played 387 games with Chris Paul in his NBA career, second behind only center DeAndre Jordan with 563 games.

The Clippers have said they plan to eventually retire Chris Paul's jersey and have the future Hall-of-Famer in the rafters of Intuit Dome, but that will clearly have to wait until the tension between both sides subsides.

articles.title: Dawson Jones' 50-yard FG on final play lifts Army over Tulsa 38-35
articles.summary: (AP) — Dawson Jones kicked a 50-yard field goal on the final play of the game and Army rallied last in a 38-35 victory over Tulsa on Friday night.Jones kicke...
articles.body:
TULSA, Okla. (AP) — Dawson Jones kicked a 50-yard field goal on the final play of the game and Army rallied last in a 38-35 victory over Tulsa on Friday night.

Jones kicked a career-long 51-yarder for a 10-7 first-quarter lead, and was good from 34 yards out to give Army (5-2, 4-1 American Conference) a 20-14 lead at halftime.

Quarterback Cale Hellums carried 30 times for 121 yards and three touchdowns for the Black Knights, while adding 64 yards on 7-for-12 passing. Godspower Nwawuihe finished with 12 rushes for 135 yards and a score.

Hellums broke free for a 41-yard touchdown on a fourth-and-1 run and Army took a 7-0 lead on the game's opening possession.

Tulsa (4-4, 1-3) answered with an 8-yard touchdown run by Javon Ross to tie it 7-all.

Ross hauled in a 17-yard scoring toss from Baylor Hayes and the Golden Hurricane led 14-10 early in the second quarter.

Hellums bulled his way in from a yard out on fourth down and Army moved ahead 17-14 thanks to a drive that lasted 15 plays and took 9:51 off the clock.

Nwawuihe raced 66 yards for a touchdown on Army's second play of the third quarter, and Zach Mundell added a two-point run for a 28-14 lead.

David Wells Jr. answered with an 11-yard touchdown run, and Trequan Jones followed with a 59-yarder to tie it 28-all heading to the fourth quarter.

Hayes connected with Jimmy Calloway for a 13-yard touchdown with 13:25 left to play to give Tulsa the lead.

Army's David Jakande blocked and recovered a punt at the Tulsa 13-yard line, and Hellums scored on a 1-yard plunge with 1:50 remaining to tie it 35-all.

Hayes totaled 262 yards on 23-for-34 passing for Tulsa, and Calloway had 10 catches for 88 yards.

articles.title: Mavericks HC Dusty May gives initial Cooper Flagg injury diagnosis after hard fall on shoulder vs. Pacers
articles.summary: The Dallas Mavericks came away from Indiana with a blowout win, but they may also be bracing for some uncertainty surrounding Cooper Flagg. Flagg exited Fri...
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks came away from Indiana with a blowout win, but they may also be bracing for some uncertainty surrounding Cooper Flagg . Flagg exited Friday night's 121-105 victory over the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse with a left shoulder injury and did not return.

After the game, head coach Dusty May gave an initial update , saying Flagg was dealing with left shoulder soreness and "will be evaluated" in the next couple of days.

The injury came with under a minute left in the first half. Flagg appeared to be headed for a breakaway dunk when Pacers swingman Aaron Nesmith fouled him hard from behind. The contact knocked Flagg off balance, and he landed awkwardly on his shoulder under the basket.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Flagg was checked by a trainer after the play. He kept rubbing his shoulder as he walked to the locker room and did not come out for the second half.

The play quickly boiled over. Naji Marshall confronted Nesmith after the foul, and players from both teams got involved in a brief shoving match along the baseline before coaches and officials separated them. Nesmith was assessed a Flagrant 1, and a double technical was handed to Nesmith and Marshall.

Before leaving, Flagg was having a terrific night. The second-year forward had 14 points, six assists, five rebounds and three steals in just 17 minutes, helping Dallas build a commanding 77-43 halftime lead. The Mavericks cruised from there without him.

Dallas will be hoping for good news on the evaluation, especially with a tough test right around the corner. The Mavericks host Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs on Saturday night at American Airlines Center, then visit the Miami Heat on Monday.

With the evaluation coming over the next couple of days, there was no immediate word on Flagg's status for the matchup with the Spurs.

Flagg, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft out of Duke, is the centerpiece of Dallas' future and a key part of May's plans in his first season leading the team . Any extended absence would be a significant blow for a Mavericks squad that looked sharp in Indiana.

For now, the Mavericks will wait on the results and hope the soreness is nothing more than that.

articles.title: Raptors’ Darko Rajakovic gives props to Toronto for tough team win over Wizards
articles.summary: Darko Rajaković has Toronto Raptors fans believing this team can win in more ways than one. That’s after guiding his squad to a gritty 112-102 road victory o...
articles.body:
Darko Rajaković has Toronto Raptors fans believing this team can win in more ways than one. That's after guiding his squad to a gritty 112-102 road victory over the Washington Wizards on Friday. Following their 43-point blowout on opening night, the Raptors faced a tougher challenge at Capital One Arena. However, they held firm down the stretch to improve to 2-0 in the 2026-27 NBA season. Rajaković praised his team's resilience after the game. He emphasized the importance of finding ways to win when shots are not falling consistently.

"The fight in finding a way to win tonight was very important," he told reporters.

Toronto backed up that mentality with a commanding performance inside. The Raptors outrebounded Washington 53-40, grabbed 19 offensive boards, and outscored the Wizards 52-32 in the paint. Scottie Barnes led the way with 28 points, 14 rebounds, and five assists. RJ Barrett contributed 23 points and nine rebounds. Kawhi Leonard added 16 points, nine boards, and three steals in 28 minutes. Toronto also received a major lift from its bench. Collin Murray-Boyles finished plus-21, and Ja'Kobe Walter posted a plus-19. The victory showcased Rajaković's ability to adapt his approach and keep his team composed when the game turned into a physical grind.

Rajaković enters his fourth season as Toronto's head coach with a fresh multi-year extension and renewed expectations. His high-movement offensive system produced a 43-point opening-night rout of Chicago. Friday's performance, though, showed the Raptors can also prevail through rebounding, defense, and second-chance opportunities. Rajaković has Toronto off to an encouraging start. They now face another early test against Anthony Edwards and the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday.
